Scattergl traces

Source: R/zz-gen-figure.R, R/zz-gen-scattergl.R
go_scattergl.Rd

The data visualized as scatter point or lines is set in `x` and `y` using the WebGL plotting engine. Bubble charts are achieved by setting `marker.size` and/or `marker.color` to a numerical arrays.

Arguments

fig

A go_figure object.

...

Further properties, including nested properties in "magic underscore" form, e.g. marker_size = 10 for marker = list(size = 10). Property values may be one-sided formulas, evaluated in data for add_*() functions.

data

A data frame in which formula properties (e.g. x = ~col, marker_size = ~col) are evaluated. Default: the data given to go_figure(). Only the evaluated values are added to the trace.

connectgaps

Determines whether or not gaps (i.e. {nan} or missing values) in the provided data arrays are connected. Logical.

customdata

Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, "scatter" traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

dx

Sets the x coordinate step. See `x0` for more info. Number.

dy

Sets the y coordinate step. See `y0` for more info. Number.

error_x

Named list or go_scattergl_error_x() object.

error_y

Named list or go_scattergl_error_y() object.

fill

Sets the area to fill with a solid color. Defaults to "none" unless this trace is stacked, then it gets "tonexty" ("tonextx") if `orientation` is "v" ("h") Use with `fillcolor` if not "none". "tozerox" and "tozeroy" fill to x=0 and y=0 respectively. "tonextx" and "tonexty" fill between the endpoints of this trace and the endpoints of the trace before it, connecting those endpoints with straight lines (to make a stacked area graph); if there is no trace before it, they behave like "tozerox" and "tozeroy". "toself" connects the endpoints of the trace (or each segment of the trace if it has gaps) into a closed shape. "tonext" fills the space between two traces if one completely encloses the other (eg consecutive contour lines), and behaves like "toself" if there is no trace before it. "tonext" should not be used if one trace does not enclose the other. Traces in a `stackgroup` will only fill to (or be filled to) other traces in the same group. With multiple `stackgroup`s or some traces stacked and some not, if fill-linked traces are not already consecutive, the later ones will be pushed down in the drawing order. One of "none", "tozeroy", "tozerox", "tonexty", "tonextx", "toself", "tonext".

fillcolor

Sets the fill color. Defaults to a half-transparent variant of the line color, marker color, or marker line color, whichever is available. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

hoverinfo

Determines what trace information appears on hover. If `none` or `skip` are set, no information is displayed upon hovering. But, if `none` is set, click and hover events are still fired. Any combination of "x", "y", "z", "text", "name" joined with "+", or one of "all", "none", "skip", or a vector of these.

hoverlabel

Named list or go_scattergl_hoverlabel() object.

hovertemplate

Template string used for rendering the information that appear on hover box. Note that this will override `hoverinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}" as well as %{xother}, {%_xother}, {%_xother_}, {%xother_}. When showing info for several points, "xother" will be added to those with different x positions from the first point. An underscore before or after "(x|y)other" will add a space on that side, only when this field is shown. Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. The variables available in `hovertemplate` are the ones emitted as event data described at this link https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-events/#event-data. Additionally, all attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. Anything contained in tag `<extra>` is displayed in the secondary box, for example `<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>`. To hide the secondary box completely, use an empty tag `<extra></extra>`. String, or a vector of these.

hovertemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

hovertext

Sets hover text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. To be seen, trace `hoverinfo` must contain a "text" flag. String, or a vector of these.

ids

Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

legend

Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are "legend", "legend2", "legend3", etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc. Subplot id: "legend", "legend2", "legend3", ....

legendgroup

Sets the legend group for this trace. Traces and shapes part of the same legend group hide/show at the same time when toggling legend items. String.

legendgrouptitle

Named list or go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle() object.

legendrank

Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with "reversed" `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout. Number.

legendwidth

Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

line

go_scattergl(): Named list or go_scattergl_line() object.

go_scattergl_marker(): Named list or go_scattergl_marker_line() object.

marker

go_scattergl(): Named list or go_scattergl_marker() object.

go_scattergl_selected(): Named list or go_scattergl_selected_marker() object.

go_scattergl_unselected(): Named list or go_scattergl_unselected_marker() object.

meta

Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index. Any value.

mode

Determines the drawing mode for this scatter trace. Any combination of "lines", "markers", "text" joined with "+", or one of "none".

name

go_scattergl(): Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. String.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickformatstop(): When used in a template, named items are created in the output figure in addition to any items the figure already has in this array. You can modify these items in the output figure by making your own item with `templateitemname` matching this `name` alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). Has no effect outside of a template. String.

opacity

go_scattergl(): Sets the opacity of the trace. Number in the interval [0, 1].

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the marker opacity. Number in the interval [0, 1], or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_selected_marker(): Sets the marker opacity of selected points. Number in the interval [0, 1].

go_scattergl_unselected_marker(): Sets the marker opacity of unselected points, applied only when a selection exists. Number in the interval [0, 1].

selected

Named list or go_scattergl_selected() object.

selectedpoints

Array containing integer indices of selected points. Has an effect only for traces that support selections. Note that an empty array means an empty selection where the `unselected` are turned on for all points, whereas, any other non-array values means no selection all where the `selected` and `unselected` styles have no effect. Any value.

showlegend

Determines whether or not an item corresponding to this trace is shown in the legend. Logical.

text

go_scattergl(): Sets text elements associated with each (x,y) pair. If a single string, the same string appears over all the data points. If an array of string, the items are mapped in order to the this trace's (x,y) coordinates. If trace `hoverinfo` contains a "text" flag and "hovertext" is not set, these elements will be seen in the hover labels. String, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle(): Sets the title of the legend group. String.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title(): Sets the title of the color bar. String.

textfont

go_scattergl(): Sets the text font. Named list or go_scattergl_textfont() object.

go_scattergl_selected(): Named list or go_scattergl_selected_textfont() object.

go_scattergl_unselected(): Named list or go_scattergl_unselected_textfont() object.

textposition

Sets the positions of the `text` elements with respects to the (x,y) coordinates. One of "top left", "top center", "top right", "middle left", "middle center", "middle right", "bottom left", "bottom center", "bottom right", or a vector of these.

texttemplate

Template string used for rendering the information text that appears on points. Note that this will override `textinfo`. Variables are inserted using %{variable}, for example "y: %{y}". Numbers are formatted using d3-format's syntax %{variable:d3-format}, for example "Price: %{y:$.2f}". https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format for details on the formatting syntax. Dates are formatted using d3-time-format's syntax %{variable|d3-time-format}, for example "Day: %{2019-01-01|%A}". https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format for details on the date formatting syntax. Variables that can't be found will be replaced with the specifier. For example, a template of "data: %{x}, %{y}" will result in a value of "data: 1, %{y}" if x is 1 and y is missing. Variables with an undefined value will be replaced with the fallback value. All attributes that can be specified per-point (the ones that are `arrayOk: true`) are available. String, or a vector of these.

texttemplatefallback

Fallback string that's displayed when a variable referenced in a template is missing. If the boolean value 'false' is passed in, the specifier with the missing variable will be displayed. Any value.

uid

Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions. String.

uirevision

Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves. Any value.

unselected

Named list or go_scattergl_unselected() object.

visible

go_scattergl(): Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If "legendonly", the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible). One of "legendonly", TRUE, FALSE.

go_scattergl_error_x(), go_scattergl_error_y(): Determines whether or not this set of error bars is visible. Logical.

x

go_scattergl(): Sets the x coordinates. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar(): Sets the x position with respect to `xref` of the color bar (in plot fraction). When `xref` is "paper", defaults to 1.02 when `orientation` is "v" and 0.5 when `orientation` is "h". When `xref` is "container", defaults to 1 when `orientation` is "v" and 0.5 when `orientation` is "h". Must be between 0 and 1 if `xref` is "container" and between "-2" and 3 if `xref` is "paper". Number.

x0

Alternate to `x`. Builds a linear space of x coordinates. Use with `dx` where `x0` is the starting coordinate and `dx` the step. Any value.

xaxis

Sets a reference between this trace's x coordinates and a 2D cartesian x axis. If "x" (the default value), the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis`. If "x2", the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis2`, and so on. Subplot id: "x", "x2", "x3", ....

xcalendar

Sets the calendar system to use with `x` date data. One of "chinese", "coptic", "discworld", "ethiopian", "gregorian", "hebrew", "islamic", "jalali", "julian", "mayan", "nanakshahi", "nepali", "persian", "taiwan", "thai", "ummalqura".

xhoverformat

Sets the hover text formatting rule for `x` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, "2016-10-13 09:15:23.456" with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would display "09~15~23.46"By default the values are formatted using `xaxis.hoverformat`. String.

xperiod

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or "M<n>" on the x axis. Special values in the form of "M<n>" could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer. Any value.

xperiod0

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the x0 axis. When `x0period` is round number of weeks, the `x0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01. Any value.

xperiodalignment

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the alignment of data points on the x axis. One of "start", "middle", "end".

y

go_scattergl(): Sets the y coordinates. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar(): Sets the y position with respect to `yref` of the color bar (in plot fraction). When `yref` is "paper", defaults to 0.5 when `orientation` is "v" and 1.02 when `orientation` is "h". When `yref` is "container", defaults to 0.5 when `orientation` is "v" and 1 when `orientation` is "h". Must be between 0 and 1 if `yref` is "container" and between "-2" and 3 if `yref` is "paper". Number.

y0

Alternate to `y`. Builds a linear space of y coordinates. Use with `dy` where `y0` is the starting coordinate and `dy` the step. Any value.

yaxis

Sets a reference between this trace's y coordinates and a 2D cartesian y axis. If "y" (the default value), the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis`. If "y2", the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis2`, and so on. Subplot id: "y", "y2", "y3", ....

ycalendar

Sets the calendar system to use with `y` date data. One of "chinese", "coptic", "discworld", "ethiopian", "gregorian", "hebrew", "islamic", "jalali", "julian", "mayan", "nanakshahi", "nepali", "persian", "taiwan", "thai", "ummalqura".

yhoverformat

Sets the hover text formatting rule for `y` using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, "2016-10-13 09:15:23.456" with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would display "09~15~23.46"By default the values are formatted using `yaxis.hoverformat`. String.

yperiod

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the period positioning in milliseconds or "M<n>" on the y axis. Special values in the form of "M<n>" could be used to declare the number of months. In this case `n` must be a positive integer. Any value.

yperiod0

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the base for period positioning in milliseconds or date string on the y0 axis. When `y0period` is round number of weeks, the `y0period0` by default would be on a Sunday i.e. 2000-01-02, otherwise it would be at 2000-01-01. Any value.

yperiodalignment

Only relevant when the axis `type` is "date". Sets the alignment of data points on the y axis. One of "start", "middle", "end".

row

Subplot grid row (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

col

Subplot grid column (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

secondary_y

If TRUE, use the secondary y axis of the subplot.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from (constructors). Named arguments take precedence.

array

Sets the data corresponding the length of each error bar. Values are plotted relative to the underlying data. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

arrayminus

Sets the data corresponding the length of each error bar in the bottom (left) direction for vertical (horizontal) bars Values are plotted relative to the underlying data. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

color

go_scattergl_error_x(), go_scattergl_error_y(): Sets the stroke color of the error bars. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(), go_scattergl_textfont(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_line(): Sets the line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the marker color. It accepts either a specific color or an array of numbers that are mapped to the colorscale relative to the max and min values of the array or relative to `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` if set. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a number mapped to a color by scattergl.marker.colorscale, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the marker.line color. It accepts either a specific color or an array of numbers that are mapped to the colorscale relative to the max and min values of the array or relative to `marker.line.cmin` and `marker.line.cmax` if set. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a number mapped to a color by scattergl.marker.line.colorscale, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_selected_marker(): Sets the marker color of selected points. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_selected_textfont(): Sets the text font color of selected points. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_unselected_marker(): Sets the marker color of unselected points, applied only when a selection exists. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_scattergl_unselected_textfont(): Sets the text font color of unselected points, applied only when a selection exists. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

copy_ystyle

Logical.

symmetric

Determines whether or not the error bars have the same length in both direction (top/bottom for vertical bars, left/right for horizontal bars. Logical.

thickness

go_scattergl_error_x(), go_scattergl_error_y(): Sets the thickness (in px) of the error bars. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar(): Sets the thickness of the color bar This measure excludes the size of the padding, ticks and labels. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

traceref

Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

tracerefminus

Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

type

Determines the rule used to generate the error bars. If "constant", the bar lengths are of a constant value. Set this constant in `value`. If "percent", the bar lengths correspond to a percentage of underlying data. Set this percentage in `value`. If "sqrt", the bar lengths correspond to the square of the underlying data. If "data", the bar lengths are set with data set `array`. One of "percent", "constant", "sqrt", "data".

value

go_scattergl_error_x(), go_scattergl_error_y(): Sets the value of either the percentage (if `type` is set to "percent") or the constant (if `type` is set to "constant") corresponding to the lengths of the error bars. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickformatstop(): string - dtickformat for described zoom level, the same as "tickformat" String.

valueminus

Sets the value of either the percentage (if `type` is set to "percent") or the constant (if `type` is set to "constant") corresponding to the lengths of the error bars in the bottom (left) direction for vertical (horizontal) bars Number in the interval [0, Inf].

width

go_scattergl_error_x(), go_scattergl_error_y(): Sets the width (in px) of the cross-bar at both ends of the error bars. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

go_scattergl_line(): Sets the line width (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the width (in px) of the lines bounding the marker points. Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

align

Sets the horizontal alignment of the text content within hover label box. Has an effect only if the hover label text spans two or more lines One of "left", "right", "auto", or a vector of these.

bgcolor

go_scattergl_hoverlabel(): Sets the background color of the hover labels for this trace Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar(): Sets the color of padded area. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

bordercolor

go_scattergl_hoverlabel(): Sets the border color of the hover labels for this trace. Color: a CSS color string or R color name, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar(): Sets the axis line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

font

go_scattergl_hoverlabel(): Sets the font used in hover labels. Named list or go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font() object.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle(): Sets this legend group's title font. Named list or go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font() object.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title(): Sets this color bar's title font. Named list or go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font() object.

namelength

Sets the default length (in number of characters) of the trace name in the hover labels for all traces. -1 shows the whole name regardless of length. 0-3 shows the first 0-3 characters, and an integer >3 will show the whole name if it is less than that many characters, but if it is longer, will truncate to `namelength - 3` characters and add an ellipsis. Integer in the interval [-1, Inf], or a vector of these.

showarrow

Sets whether or not to show the hover label arrow/triangle pointing to the data point. Logical.

family

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(), go_scattergl_textfont(): HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String.

lineposition

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(): Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none", or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none".

shadow

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(): Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String, or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String.

size

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(), go_scattergl_textfont(): Number in the interval [1, Inf], or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Number in the interval [1, Inf].

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the marker size (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_selected_marker(): Sets the marker size of selected points. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

go_scattergl_unselected_marker(): Sets the marker size of unselected points, applied only when a selection exists. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

style

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(), go_scattergl_textfont(): Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic", or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic".

textcase

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(): Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower", or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower".

variant

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(): Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase", or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase".

go_scattergl_textfont(): Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", or a vector of these.

weight

go_scattergl_hoverlabel_font(): Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000], or a vector of these.

go_scattergl_legendgrouptitle_font(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont(), go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font(): Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000].

go_scattergl_textfont(): Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. One of "normal", "bold", or a vector of these.

dash

Sets the style of the lines. One of "dash", "dashdot", "dot", "longdash", "longdashdot", "solid".

shape

Determines the line shape. The values correspond to step-wise line shapes. One of "linear", "hv", "vh", "hvh", "vhv".

angle

Sets the marker angle in respect to `angleref`. Angle in degrees, or a vector of these.

autocolorscale

go_scattergl_marker(): Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `marker.colorscale`. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed. Logical.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `marker.line.colorscale`. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed. Logical.

cauto

go_scattergl_marker(): Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here in `marker.color`) or the bounds set in `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Defaults to `false` when `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` are set by the user. Logical.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here in `marker.line.color`) or the bounds set in `marker.line.cmin` and `marker.line.cmax` Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. Defaults to `false` when `marker.line.cmin` and `marker.line.cmax` are set by the user. Logical.

cmax

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmin` must be set as well. Number.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.line.color` and if set, `marker.line.cmin` must be set as well. Number.

cmid

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `marker.cmin` and/or `marker.cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color`. Has no effect when `marker.cauto` is `false`. Number.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `marker.line.cmin` and/or `marker.line.cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.line.color`. Has no effect when `marker.line.cauto` is `false`. Number.

cmin

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.color` and if set, `marker.cmax` must be set as well. Number.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as in `marker.line.color` and if set, `marker.line.cmax` must be set as well. Number.

coloraxis

Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are "coloraxis", "coloraxis2", "coloraxis3", etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis. Subplot id: "coloraxis", "coloraxis2", "coloraxis3", ....

colorbar

Named list or go_scattergl_marker_colorbar() object.

colorscale

go_scattergl_marker(): Sets the colorscale. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd. Colorscale: a vector of colors, a two-column data.frame of (value, color), or the name of a sequential, diverging or cyclical scale in px_colors() (append "_r" to reverse).

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Sets the colorscale. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `marker.line.cmin` and `marker.line.cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd. Colorscale: a vector of colors, a two-column data.frame of (value, color), or the name of a sequential, diverging or cyclical scale in px_colors() (append "_r" to reverse).

reversescale

go_scattergl_marker(): Reverses the color mapping if true. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. If true, `marker.cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `marker.cmax` will correspond to the first color. Logical.

go_scattergl_marker_line(): Reverses the color mapping if true. Has an effect only if in `marker.line.color` is set to a numerical array. If true, `marker.line.cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `marker.line.cmax` will correspond to the first color. Logical.

showscale

Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace. Has an effect only if in `marker.color` is set to a numerical array. Logical.

sizemin

Has an effect only if `marker.size` is set to a numerical array. Sets the minimum size (in px) of the rendered marker points. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

sizeref

Has an effect only if `marker.size` is set to a numerical array. Sets the scale factor used to determine the rendered size of marker points. Use with `sizemin` and `sizemode`. Number.

orientation

Sets the orientation of the colorbar. One of "h", "v".

outlinecolor

Sets the axis line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

outlinewidth

Sets the width (in px) of the axis line. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

separatethousands

If "true", even 4-digit integers are separated Logical.

showexponent

If "all", all exponents are shown besides their significands. If "first", only the exponent of the first tick is shown. If "last", only the exponent of the last tick is shown. If "none", no exponents appear. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

showticklabels

Determines whether or not the tick labels are drawn. Logical.

showtickprefix

If "all", all tick labels are displayed with a prefix. If "first", only the first tick is displayed with a prefix. If "last", only the last tick is displayed with a suffix. If "none", tick prefixes are hidden. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

showticksuffix

Same as `showtickprefix` but for tick suffixes. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

thicknessmode

Determines whether this color bar's thickness (i.e. the measure in the constant color direction) is set in units of plot "fraction" or in "pixels". Use `thickness` to set the value. One of "fraction", "pixels".

tick0

Sets the placement of the first tick on this axis. Use with `dtick`. If the axis `type` is "log", then you must take the log of your starting tick (e.g. to set the starting tick to 100, set the `tick0` to 2) except when `dtick`="L<f>" (see `dtick` for more info). If the axis `type` is "date", it should be a date string, like date data. If the axis `type` is "category", it should be a number, using the scale where each category is assigned a serial number from zero in the order it appears. Any value.

tickangle

Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the horizontal. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the tick labels vertically. Angle in degrees.

tickcolor

Sets the tick color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

tickfont

Sets the color bar's tick label font Named list or go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickfont() object.

tickformat

Sets the tick label formatting rule using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, "2016-10-13 09:15:23.456" with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would display "09~15~23.46" String.

tickformatstops

List of named lists or go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickformatstop() objects.

ticklabeloverflow

Determines how we handle tick labels that would overflow either the graph div or the domain of the axis. The default value for inside tick labels is "hide past domain". In other cases the default is "hide past div". One of "allow", "hide past div", "hide past domain".

ticklabelposition

Determines where tick labels are drawn relative to the ticks. Left and right options are used when `orientation` is "h", top and bottom when `orientation` is "v". One of "outside", "inside", "outside top", "inside top", "outside left", "inside left", "outside right", "inside right", "outside bottom", "inside bottom".

ticklabelstep

Sets the spacing between tick labels as compared to the spacing between ticks. A value of 1 (default) means each tick gets a label. A value of 2 means shows every 2nd label. A larger value n means only every nth tick is labeled. `tick0` determines which labels are shown. Not implemented for axes with `type` "log" or "multicategory", or when `tickmode` is "array". Integer in the interval [1, Inf].

ticklen

Sets the tick length (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

tickmode

Sets the tick mode for this axis. If "auto", the number of ticks is set via `nticks`. If "linear", the placement of the ticks is determined by a starting position `tick0` and a tick step `dtick` ("linear" is the default value if `tick0` and `dtick` are provided). If "array", the placement of the ticks is set via `tickvals` and the tick text is `ticktext`. ("array" is the default value if `tickvals` is provided). One of "auto", "linear", "array".

tickprefix

Sets a tick label prefix. String.

ticks

Determines whether ticks are drawn or not. If **, this axis' ticks are not drawn. If "outside" ("inside"), this axis' are drawn outside (inside) the axis lines. One of "outside", "inside", "".

ticksuffix

Sets a tick label suffix. String.

ticktext

Sets the text displayed at the ticks position via `tickvals`. Only has an effect if `tickmode` is set to "array". Used with `tickvals`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

tickvals

Sets the values at which ticks on this axis appear. Only has an effect if `tickmode` is set to "array". Used with `ticktext`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

tickwidth

Sets the tick width (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

title

String (the title text), named list or go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title() object.

xanchor

Sets this color bar's horizontal position anchor. This anchor binds the `x` position to the "left", "center" or "right" of the color bar. Defaults to "left" when `orientation` is "v" and "center" when `orientation` is "h". One of "left", "center", "right".

xpad

Sets the amount of padding (in px) along the x direction. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

xref

Sets the container `x` refers to. "container" spans the entire `width` of the plot. "paper" refers to the width of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

yanchor

Sets this color bar's vertical position anchor This anchor binds the `y` position to the "top", "middle" or "bottom" of the color bar. Defaults to "middle" when `orientation` is "v" and "bottom" when `orientation` is "h". One of "top", "middle", "bottom".

ypad

Sets the amount of padding (in px) along the y direction. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

yref

Sets the container `y` refers to. "container" spans the entire `height` of the plot. "paper" refers to the height of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

dtickrange

range ["min", "max"], where "min", "max" - dtick values which describe some zoom level, it is possible to omit "min" or "max" value by passing "null" Vector or list of 2 element(s).

enabled

Determines whether or not this stop is used. If `false`, this stop is ignored even within its `dtickrange`. Logical.

templateitemname

Used to refer to a named item in this array in the template. Named items from the template will be created even without a matching item in the input figure, but you can modify one by making an item with `templateitemname` matching its `name`, alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). If there is no template or no matching item, this item will be hidden unless you explicitly show it with `visible: true`. String.

side

Determines the location of color bar's title with respect to the color bar. Defaults to "top" when `orientation` is "v" and defaults to "right" when `orientation` is "h". One of "right", "top", "bottom".

Value

Each go_*() function returns a graph object of the same class as its name; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_scattergl() and the nested object constructors below create validated graph objects (named lists). Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when an object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify()). add_scattergl() creates an object and adds it to a figure.

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_tickformatstop()

go_scattergl_marker_colorbar_title_font()

scattergl.marker.colorbar.title.font: Sets this color bar's title font.

go_scattergl_marker_line()

Examples

go_scattergl(x = 1:3, y = c(2, 1, 3), mode = "markers", marker_color = "red")

#> {

#>   "mode": "markers",
#>   "x": [
#>     1,
#>     2,
#>     3
#>   ],
#>   "y": [
#>     2,
#>     1,
#>     3
#>   ],
#>   "marker": {
#>     "color": "red"
#>   }
#> }
#>
